review.title: Nhận xét bài viết trên lớp
paragraphs: Some people think students having the best academic performances should be rewarded by school, others argue that hard-work and showing great improvement ones are more deserve to these gifts. Personally, I strongly believe that both top and high-motivation students have abilities to be rewarded.

On the one hand, admittedly, rewarding top-grade students is undeniably justified. Initially, having diligently applied themselves to their studies, those students deserve their praises and privileges, which may encourages they and others to study harder to win the rewards, propel overall academic gains. Furthermore, this kind of competition is seen in almost every aspect of life, where only the best individual are rewarded. Being used to this reality and thriving in the face of fierce competition, students are able to achieve success in later life.

On the other hand, however, it is equally important to rewarding students having significant developments. Firstly, since only a few smart students can come first and receive the rewards, others may think that their effort is futile. Because they can not surpass those outstanding individuals, they prone to feeling overwhelmed and disheartened and gradually lose the incentive to study. Moreover, emphasizing improvements, school can encourage all student to be diligent in their studies and help them to understand what they need to constantly improve themselves, irrespective of how well they have been or are performing. The constant desire to outdo themselves is even benefit themselves more than the competitive determination to win against all others.
In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that school should reward not only the best students but also others thriving in their studies.

Some people think that school should reward students who show the best academic results, while others believe that it is more important to reward students who show improvements.
Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
